source.title: Automated Learning Rate Scheduler for Large-batch Training
source.authors: Chiheon Kim; Saehoon Kim; Jongmin Kim; Donghoon Lee; Sungwoong Kim

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices; no material garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out classification accuracy across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets, and reports how alternative learning-rate schedules change the large-batch outcome.
record.gate_note: The study reports test or validation accuracy for models trained with fixed epoch budgets and multiple batch sizes. These results bear on V5. The paper's generalization-gap framing is contextual; it does not report paired training and test error gaps as its main measure.
record.test_reason: Fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons and learning-rate schedule interventions directly test V5's large-batch penalty and recipe-dependent mitigation. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: AutoWU automates warmup and learning-rate selection and is claimed to deliver performance comparable to or better than tuned schedules. The strongest demonstrated reductions in large-batch accuracy loss concern CIFAR-100 with AdamP and ImageNet ResNet-50. The tables qualify that broad claim: LAMB and the additional architectures often perform worse with AutoWU. The authors do not demonstrate universal elimination of the small-versus-large-batch penalty.
record.recipe_differences: Tests large-batch training at fixed epoch budgets with AdamP or LAMB and compares a conventional warmup-plus-cosine schedule with an automated warmup and decay schedule. It does not compare small and large batches under a broad set of otherwise identical, universally tuned recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size, optimizer, architecture, dataset, decay schedule, and warmup growth/fraction affect reported performance. The paper reports AutoWU's linear warmup is sensitive to ηmax; changing ρw also changes performance.
record.peer_reviewed: 8th ICML Workshop on Automated Machine Learning (2021)
record.problems: ImageNet results are single runs with a fixed random seed due to resource constraints. The study reports test/validation accuracy rather than paired training and test error gaps. It tests only image classification, and comparisons include tuned baseline schedules whose performance depends on hyperparameter choices.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted nonessential batch-size/schedule combinations from Tables 1–3, including CIFAR results at intermediate batch sizes and LAMB and AutoWU values not needed to show the version's pattern or exceptions. Also omitted validation-accuracy sweeps and warmup ablations in Figures 5–7 and Table 4; these concern schedule tuning rather than a separate batch-size generalization result. The paper states several figure results in text, but the full figure-only curves are not cataloged.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited or broader tuning. Comparing AdamP and LAMB does not supply that contrast.

Language models; extending training beyond the fixed epoch budget; normalization or regularization interventions. All baseline schedules already include learning-rate scaling and warmup, so their benefit over an unadapted recipe is not isolated.
Dropout interventions and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to V5 as measurements or necessary references. A residual large-batch penalty is not automatically partial: V5 specifies worse held-out performance without requiring a particular penalty magnitude. AutoWU failures do not challenge a claim that recipe changes can help in some settings. Omitted table combinations and ablations are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. No paired training–test gap is required to test V5. ImageNet results are single runs; CIFAR results report three-run standard deviations.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD.
Language models; explicit comparison of training and test error gaps; normalization or regularization changes to the recipe.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.
